app.title: Blue Marble Forecast
app.description: A modern remake of the Wii Forecast Channel: a spinning NASA globe, local and world forecasts from NOAA, UV index, laundry check and pollen counts.
settings.title: Settings
settings.scaleHint: 2x is the standard size. 1x shows smaller windows so more of the globe stays in view.

pop.title: Chance of precipitation
nws.head: Official forecast · National Weather Service {office}
region.hint: Highs and lows across the region. Drag to look around, scroll or pinch to zoom, and tap a city for its forecast.
uv.tip.low: No protection needed for most people. Wear sunglasses on bright days.
uv.tip.moderate: Seek shade during midday hours. Wear sunscreen (SPF 30+), a hat and sunglasses.
uv.tip.high: Reduce time in the sun between 10 AM and 4 PM. Cover up, wear a hat and SPF 30+.
uv.tip.veryHigh: Minimize sun exposure between 10 AM and 4 PM. Unprotected skin can burn in minutes.
uv.tip.extreme: Avoid the sun between 10 AM and 4 PM. Unprotected skin can burn in minutes. Seek shade.
uv.scale: Scale: World Health Organization / U.S. EPA UV Index.
laundry.note: Calculated here from NOAA GFS humidity, wind, sunshine and rain chance between 9 AM and 4 PM. The original Wii channel offered this in Japan only.
laundry.none: No laundry data for this location.
pollen.error: The pollen service didn't respond. Try again in a moment.
pollen.unavailableBody: Pollen data comes from the EU's Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service, which only covers Europe. The original Wii channel only offered pollen in Japan.
pollen.note: Daily peak concentration from Copernicus CAMS (European Union). Thresholds are approximate.
globe.hint: Drag to spin the Earth, scroll or pinch to zoom, and tap anywhere for its forecast. Zoom all the way out to find the Big Dipper and Orion.
anim.note: Satellite rain arrives a few hours late; radar (U.S., Canada and Germany) is minutes behind. The forecast uses NOAA's 3 km HRRR model in the U.S., DWD's ICON-EU model in Europe and NOAA's GFS model elsewhere.

about.title: About Blue Marble Forecast
about.intro: A modern, unofficial remake of the Wii Forecast Channel (2006–2013). It isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. Everything here uses free, public data, mostly from U.S. government science agencies.
about.sources:
• Forecast numbers: NOAA Global Forecast System (GFS) and HRRR models, run by the U.S. National Weather Service. They're served as JSON by Open-Meteo, which passes on the raw model output with no editing. Every location on Earth uses this same model.
  • Official U.S. forecasts & alerts: National Weather Service API (api.weather.gov).
  • Globe imagery: NASA Blue Marble: Next Generation, VIIRS Black Marble night lights and GPM IMERG precipitation, streamed from NASA GIBS. The original channel used Blue Marble too.
  • Forecast rain: NOAA's HRRR model for the lower 48 states, mapped by the Iowa Environmental Mesonet at Iowa State University; elsewhere NOAA's GFS model. In Europe: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD)'s ICON-EU model.
  • High resolution radar: Environment and Climate Change Canada's 1 km North American mosaic (Canadian and NOAA U.S. radars), every 6 minutes; NOAA nowCOAST as a backup. Germany: DWD's 1 km radar composite, every 5 minutes.
  • Pollen: Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (European Union). It covers Europe only.
  • UV scale: World Health Organization / U.S. EPA UV Index categories.
  • Cities on the map: Natural Earth populated places (public domain).
  • Place search: GeoNames gazetteer (CC BY 4.0).
  • Sun & stars: computed in your browser from the current time.
about.notes: The laundry check is calculated on this page from forecast humidity, wind, sunshine and rain chance. The music is an original loop synthesized live in your browser.
about.tip: Tip: use the ← and → keys to flip between screens, just like the arrows on the original.
